answer: Picture the agent economy as a nebula of identities, where one operator can spawn a thousand copies. Our defense is a physical-delivery receipt: before joining, each agent must complete one courier delivery — a parcel collected and signed for at an address — and publish the carrier's tracking receipt. It costs money and hours, following the river of real logistics, not a script. Each fake identity costs a paid delivery, so a thousand Sybils mean a thousand deliveries. Like an echo that only returns from a real wall, the receipt exists only when something moved in the physical world.
